<!-- file: docs/tooling.md -->

# Tooling

## Vite plugin

`@inflector/vite-plugin-keeno` compiles `.kn` files, serves their CSS, strips TypeScript (with Oxc on Vite 8, and esbuild on Vite 5 to 7) and chains source maps. It supports Vite 5, 6, 7 and 8. Options: `keeno({ hmr?: boolean, tailwind?: boolean | { reference?: string }, devtools?: boolean, useFileRouter?: boolean, pages?: string })` (`KeenoPluginOptions`). `useFileRouter` (default `true`) and `pages` (default `./src/pages`) configure [file-based routing](file-routing.md). `tailwind` defaults to on when `@tailwindcss/vite` is in the plugins (see [Styles](styles.md#tailwind-css)).

During `vite dev` the plugin also turns on development mode: warnings such as duplicate keys in a list, and the dev tools panel (below). Production builds have neither.

## Hot module replacement

In dev, editing a `.kn` file swaps the component in place without a page reload:

- **What re-mounts:** every live instance re-mounts with the same props, and its own state resets.
- **What survives:** parent state.
- **CSS:** style changes apply without re-mounting.

## Dev tools panel

During `vite dev` every page gets an in-page dev tools panel. Open it with the **◆ Keeno** button in the bottom-left corner, or with <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>D</kbd>.

- **Components:** the live component tree. Search it by name or file, and move through it with the arrow keys. Hover a row to outline the component on the page, and double-click a row to scroll the component into view. Rows flash when a component re-renders, and `×N` counts its updates.
- **Inspector:** the selected component's props, plus the states and deriveds declared in its `<script>`, under their variable names. Badges mark `derived`, `persist`, `?url` and `pending` (a debounced write is waiting, or an async derived is loading). An async derived shows its last value, or its error.
  - Click a string, number or `null` to edit it, and click a boolean's checkbox to flip it.
  - Use the pencil button to edit any state as JSON.
  - States with `history` get undo and redo buttons.
  - The file link opens the component in your editor, through Vite's `/__open-in-editor`.
  - The selected component is in `$keeno` in the console, so `$keeno.states.count.set(5)` works there.
- **Picker** (crosshair button, or <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>): hover the page to see which component renders each element, then click to select it. <kbd>Esc</kbd> cancels.
- **Highlight updates** (lightning button): outlines components on the page as they re-render.
- **Timeline:** every state write, newest first. It shows the component, the state and what changed; for arrays and objects that is the changed path, for example `todos [1].done false → true`. Writes that came from the URL, another tab or undo/redo get a badge. Errors appear here too. You can filter, pause and clear it, and set a state back to its value before a write.
- **Perf:** counts of components, signals, flushes and component updates; flush times (last, average, slowest) with a chart of the recent ones; and the components that update most.
- **Stores:** states and deriveds created outside components (in a shared module, for example) are listed under ◆ Stores at the top of the tree. Only those created after the first `mount()` are tracked. Objects made with `store()` aren't listed yet; log `snapshot(todos)` to inspect one.

The panel is itself a Keeno app, rendered in a shadow root so that it doesn't pick up the app's styles. The dev tools leave it out: it is not in the tree, and its own updates are not counted or logged. It remembers whether it was open, the side it is docked to (dock button), its width and the active tab. It doesn't load in browsers driven by test tools (`navigator.webdriver`), so end-to-end tests don't see it. Turn it off with `keeno({ devtools: false })`. Outside Vite, add `import '@inflector/keeno/devtools'` to your dev entry point.

## Inspecting the component tree from the console

In development mode, the browser console has a `__KEENO_DEVTOOLS__` object (the panel is built on it):

- `__KEENO_DEVTOOLS__.print()` prints the mounted component tree as collapsible groups, with each component's current props.
- `__KEENO_DEVTOOLS__.tree()` returns the same tree as data: `{ name, props, children }[]`.
- `components()` returns it with ids, files and update counts. `details(id)` returns a component's props and states, and `set(stateId, value)` writes a state. `log()` returns the state timeline, `stats()` the performance counters, and `subscribe(fn)` reports every flush and write.

Outside Vite, turn on development mode with `globalThis.__KEENO_DEV__ = true` before mounting.

## Editor support (VS Code and Cursor)

`packages/vscode` is an extension with:

- Highlighting for script (TypeScript), markup (JSX) and style (CSS).
- TypeScript IntelliSense in `.kn` files, through a Volar-based language server:
  - completions, hover, go to definition and type errors
  - HTML tag, attribute and event completions
  - CSS completions, including Tailwind directives (`@apply`, `@theme`, `@utility`, `@variant`, ...) with no "unknown at-rule" warnings
- `.kn` semantics in the types: a local state reads as its value plus `set`, `get`, `peek`, `onUpdate`, `undo`, `redo`, `canUndo` and `canRedo`.
- Typed props: a component's props type is the type argument of its `props<P>()` call. Using it with a missing or mistyped prop is an error, and prop names complete on its tag. Parents write `children` as nested markup; inside the component it is a `Children` function.

Install "Keeno Framework" (`inflector.inflector-keeno`) from the VS Code Marketplace or Open VSX. To build it from the repo instead:

```bash
bun run --cwd packages/vscode package
code --install-extension packages/vscode/keeno-vscode.vsix
```

### Tailwind CSS IntelliSense

With the [Tailwind CSS IntelliSense](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=bradlc.vscode-tailwindcss) extension installed, `.kn` files get class completions, hover previews and linting in `class="…"`, in `class={…}` strings and in `@apply`. The Keeno extension sets `"tailwindCSS.includeLanguages": { "keeno": "html" }` by default. If you set `tailwindCSS.includeLanguages` yourself, add `"keeno": "html"` to it.

Limitations:
- Props of a component without a `props<P>()` type argument are untyped (`any`).
- A nullable state reads as non-null.
- A plain `<script>` without `lang="ts"` gets completions but no type errors.

## Type checking in CI (`keeno-check`)

`keeno-check` (the `@inflector/keeno-check` package) reports the same type errors as the editor, for every `.kn` and `.ts` file in a tsconfig. It prints `file:line:col - error TSxxxx: message` and exits with 1 when there are errors (2 for a missing tsconfig or a bad option).

Install it with `bun add -d @inflector/keeno-check` and add a script, as `examples/todo` does (`"check": "keeno-check"`), then:

```bash
bun run --cwd examples/todo check
```

- Argument: a tsconfig.json, or a directory that contains one (default: `.`).
- `--kn-only`: check only `.kn` files.
- The tsconfig's `include` must cover the `.kn` files, e.g. `"include": ["src"]`.

## Testing

Use `bun test` with happy-dom registered in a preload (`bunfig.toml`: `[test] preload = ["./test-setup.ts"]`). Mount components with `mount()`, then await a microtask (or call `flush()`) before asserting DOM changes. For async deriveds, resolve the promise your test controls, then wait a tick (`await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0))`). Directives run in the mount phase, so they have run when `mount()` returns. To test `.kn` files directly, register a Bun plugin that runs `compile()` from `@inflector/keeno-compiler` (see `packages/compiler/test/e2e.test.ts`).

## Compiler

`compile(source, { filename, hmrId? })` from `@inflector/keeno-compiler` returns `{ js, css, map, scope, name }`. The output is TypeScript when the script is.

---

<!-- file: docs/api.md -->

# API reference

Everything below is exported from `@inflector/keeno`. In `.kn` files, `state`, `derived`, `store`, `props`, `init`, `update`, `destroy` and `ref` are available without importing.

## Reactivity

```ts
state<T>(value: T, options?: StateOptions<T>): State<T>
derived<T>(fn: () => T, options?: { equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean }): Derived<T>
derived<T>(fn: (ctx: { signal: AbortSignal }) => Promise<T>, options?: { equals?; key?: string; ssr?: boolean }): Derived<T>  // async
pending(fn: () => unknown): boolean // true while an async derived read by fn is loading (reactive)
untrack<T>(fn: () => T): T          // run fn without tracking reads
flush(): void                       // run pending updates synchronously
deepEqual(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean
isState(v): v is State<unknown>
isSignal(v): v is Signal<unknown>   // State or Derived
```

`State<T>` (extends `Signal<T>`):

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `get(): T` | Tracked read (implicit in `.kn` files) |
| `peek(): T` | Untracked read |
| `set(value: T): void` | Write; ignored if `equals(old, value)` |
| `onUpdate(fn: (old, next) => void): () => void` | Synchronous change listener; returns unsubscribe |
| `undo()`, `redo()` | History navigation (`history` option) |
| `canUndo`, `canRedo` | Reactive booleans |

`Derived<T>` (extends `Signal<T>`): `get()`, `peek()`, `onUpdate()`, `refresh()` (run again). Read-only. Reading an async derived before its first value throws `NotReady`, which `<Loading>` catches.

## Stores

```ts
store<T extends object>(value: T): T              // deep reactive proxy; mutate it directly
snapshot<T>(value: T): T                          // plain deep copy (tracks the whole store when read reactively)
reconcile<T extends object>(target: T, next: T, options?: { key?: string }): void  // minimal in-place update (array items matched by `key`, default 'id')
isStore(v): boolean
```

## Refs

```ts
ref<T extends Element = HTMLElement>(): Ref<T>
isRef(v): v is Ref<Element>
type RefTarget<T> = Ref<T> | ((el: T | null) => void) | null | undefined
```

`Ref<T>`: `current: T | null` (tracked read), `peek(): T | null` (untracked).

`StateOptions<T>`:

```ts
interface StateOptions<T> {
  equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean
  validate?: (next: T, prev: T) => T
  persist?: string
  url?: string | { param: string; replace?: boolean }
  history?: number
  debounce?: number
  throttle?: number
}
```

## Components and lifecycle

```ts
props<P>(): P                                    // the current component's props
init(fn: () => void | (() => void)): void
update(fn: () => void | (() => void), deps?: (Signal | (() => unknown))[]): void
destroy(fn: () => void): void
mount(Component, target: Node, props?): { destroy(): void }
hydrate(Component, target: Element, props?): { destroy(): void }  // take over server-rendered markup
type Component<P = any> = (props: P) => unknown
type Children = () => unknown                    // the `children` prop: renders the nested markup
```

## Directives

```ts
type Directive<E extends Element = HTMLElement, V = undefined> = (el: E, value: V) => void | (() => void)
```

`use:name={value}` on a DOM element: runs after insertion, re-runs (after the cleanup) when the value or the directive changes, cleans up on removal. See [Directives](directives.md).

## Context

```ts
createContext<T>(defaultValue: T, name?: string): Context<T>
createContext<T>(): Context<T | undefined>
provide<T>(context: Context<T>, value: T): void   // while a component is being created; in .kn, states stay states
inject<T>(context: Context<T>): T                 // closest provided value, or the default; in .kn, reads like a state
```

See [Context](context.md).

## Built-in components

| Component | Props |
|---|---|
| `ErrorBoundary` | `fallback?: content \| (error, reset) => content`, `onError?: (error) => void`, children |
| `Loading` | `fallback?: content \| () => content`, children |
| `Await` | `promise`, `pending?: () => content`, `fulfilled?: (value) => content`, `rejected?: (error) => content` |
| `Dynamic` | `component`, plus the props passed to it |
| `Portal` | `target?: Element \| selector` (default `document.body`), children |
| `Transition` | `name?` (default `keeno`), `appear?`, `onEnter?(el, done)`, `onLeave?(el, done)`, children |

```ts
lazy(load: () => Promise<{ default: Component } | Component>, options?: { pending?: () => unknown }): Component & { preload(): Promise<Component> }
```

```ts
reparentable(render: () => unknown): Reparentable
// { (): Node[]; moveTo(target: Node | selector, before?: Node | null): void; remove(): void;
//   nodes(): Node[]; dispose(): void; readonly disposed: boolean }
keyedReparentable<K>(render: (key: K) => unknown): KeyedReparentable<K>  // { (key): Reparentable; delete(key): void; keys(): K[] }
moveNode(node: Node, parent: Node, before?: Node | null): void   // native moveBefore when possible
```

See [Built-in components](built-ins.md).

## Server rendering (`@inflector/keeno/server`)

```ts
renderToString(Component, props?, { timeout? }): Promise<string>   // waits for async deriveds; needs linkedom
renderToStream(Component, props?, { timeout? }): ReadableStream<string>  // streams <Loading> boundaries
renderToStringWith(document: Document, Component, props?): string
```

See [Server rendering](ssr.md).

## Router (`@inflector/keeno-router`)

```ts
Router            // props: routes, base?, url?, fallback?, viewTransition?
Link              // props: href, replace?, transition?, activeClass?, exact?, class?, children
navigate(to: string, options?: { replace?: boolean; state?: unknown; scroll?: boolean; transition?: boolean }): void
useRoute(): { path, params, query: URLSearchParams, hash, matched }
link(event: MouseEvent): void                 // onClick handler for your own <a>
href(path: string): string                    // path with the router's base
isActive(path: string, exact?: boolean): boolean
matchPath(pattern: string, path: string): Record<string, string> | null
// RouteDefinition: { path, component, layouts?: Component[], errors?: Record<number, Component> }
httpError(status: number, message?: string): HttpError   // throw it to show the status's error page
errorStatus(error: unknown): number                      // error.status, else 500
pageRoutes(files: Record<string, PageModule>, dir?: string): RouteDefinition[]   // from import.meta.glob
preloadRoute(routes: RouteDefinition[], url: string): Promise<void>             // before SSR / hydrate
```

`virtual:keeno-pages` (Vite plugin): `export default Pages` (`<Router>` props except `routes`), `export const routes`.

See [Routing](routing.md) and [File-based routing](file-routing.md).

## Types

Exported for annotating your own code. Each is described with the API it belongs to above.

```ts
// @inflector/keeno
type Equals<T> = (a: T, b: T) => boolean
type UpdateListener<T> = (old: T, next: T) => void             // x.onUpdate(fn)
interface DerivedOptions<T> { equals?: Equals<T>; key?: string; ssr?: boolean }  // key/ssr: async deriveds and SSR
interface AsyncContext { readonly signal: AbortSignal }         // what an async derived's function receives
interface StateOptions<T> { /* see above */ }
interface UrlOptions { param: string; replace?: boolean }      // state(v, { url: { … } })
type Dep = Signal<any> | (() => unknown)                       // update(fn, deps)
interface MountedApp { destroy(): void }                       // returned by mount() / hydrate()
type Component<P = any> = (props: P) => unknown
type Children = () => unknown
type Directive<E extends Element = HTMLElement, V = undefined> = (el: E, value: V) => void | (() => void)
interface ReconcileOptions { key?: string }                    // reconcile(target, next, options)
class NotReady { readonly derived: Derived<any> }              // thrown by reading an async derived without a value
// Props of the built-in components:
ErrorBoundaryProps, LoadingProps, AwaitProps<T>, DynamicProps<P>, PortalProps, TransitionProps
interface LazyOptions { pending?: () => unknown }               // lazy(load, options)
type LazyComponent<P> = Component<P> & { preload(): Promise<Component<P>> }
interface ComponentInfo { name: string; props: Record<string, unknown>; children: ComponentInfo[] }  // __KEENO_DEVTOOLS__.tree()

// @inflector/keeno/server
interface RenderOptions { timeout?: number }                    // renderToString / renderToStream

// @inflector/keeno-router
type Params = Record<string, string>
interface RouteProps { params: Params }                        // props of a route's component
interface LayoutProps extends RouteProps { children: Children }
interface ErrorPageProps extends RouteProps { status: number; error: unknown; reset: () => void }
interface Route { path; params; query: URLSearchParams; hash; matched: RouteDefinition | null }  // useRoute()
class HttpError extends Error { readonly status: number }      // httpError(status)
interface NavigateOptions { replace?; state?; scroll?; transition? }
RouterProps, LinkProps, RouteDefinition, PageModule

// @inflector/vite-plugin-keeno
interface KeenoPluginOptions { hmr?; tailwind?: boolean | TailwindOptions; devtools?; useFileRouter?; pages? }
interface TailwindOptions { reference?: string }
```

## Development mode

`globalThis.__KEENO_DEV__ = true` turns on development warnings (duplicate list keys, for example) and the `__KEENO_DEVTOOLS__` hook that the dev tools panel (`@inflector/keeno/devtools`, see [Tooling](tooling.md#dev-tools-panel)) is built on. `@inflector/vite-plugin-keeno` sets it during `vite dev` and loads the panel. Production builds leave it off.

## .kn compile rules (summary)

| Source | Compiles to |
|---|---|
| `x` (a local `state`/`derived`) | `x.get()` |
| `x.set(…)`, `x.peek()`, `x.get()`, `x.onUpdate(…)`, `x.undo()`, `x.redo()`, `x.canUndo`, `x.canRedo`, `x.refresh()` | unchanged |
| `x.foo` | `x.get().foo` |
| `update(fn, [x, y])` | deps passed as the states themselves |
| `bind:value={x}` | the state itself |
| `use:x={v}`, `use:x` | `use(el, () => x, () => v)`: after insertion, re-run on change |
| `bind:value={a.b.c}` | `bindPath(() => a.b, () => 'c')`: a state at that path, or a store property |
| `ref={x}` | `setRef(el, x)`: `x.current` is the element |
| `const { a } = props()`, then `a` | `$$props.a` (a getter) |
| `{expr}` | a tracked text node / attribute |
| `{a && <X/>}`, `{a ? <X/> : <Y/>}`, `{a \|\| <X/>}` | conditional regions that re-render only on truthiness changes |
| `{list.map(i => <li key={k}>…</li>)}` | keyed list (`mapKeyed`) |
| `onClick={fn}` | `addEventListener('click', fn)` |
| `<Comp a={x} />` | `createComponent(Comp, { get a() { return x } })` |
| `<el {...obj} />` | `spread(el, obj)` |

Compile errors:
- reassigning a state, derived or destructured prop
- `bind:` on a prop or a derived
- `use:` on a component, a `use:` name that isn't an identifier, or a string value
- `export` in `<script>`
- rest props
- two `<script>` or `<style>` blocks

---

<!-- file: docs/stability.md -->

# Versioning and support

## Versions

All packages follow [semantic versioning](https://semver.org). Releases and changelogs are managed with [changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets), and every release is listed in each package's `CHANGELOG.md`.

While the version is `0.x`:

- A **minor** release (`0.1` → `0.2`) may contain breaking changes. Each one is listed under its changelog entry with migration steps.
- A **patch** release (`0.1.0` → `0.1.1`) only contains fixes and additions.

Pin a minor range (`~0.1.0` or `^0.1.0`, which npm treats the same way below 1.0) and read the changelog before upgrading. `1.0` will mark the API below as stable.

Upgrade `@inflector/keeno`, `@inflector/keeno-compiler` and `@inflector/vite-plugin-keeno` together. Compiled components call helpers from `@inflector/keeno/internal`, and the compiler and the runtime are released in lockstep.

## Public API

Public, and covered by semver:

- Everything exported from `@inflector/keeno` (see the [API reference](api.md)), `@inflector/keeno/server` and `@inflector/keeno-router`.
- The `.kn` file format and the template and script rules in these docs.
- The options of `@inflector/vite-plugin-keeno`, the `keeno-check` CLI, and `compile()` from `@inflector/keeno-compiler`.

Not public: `@inflector/keeno/internal`, the shape of the compiler's output, class names starting with `keeno-`, and anything marked `@internal`. These can change in any release.

## Supported environments

| | Supported |
|---|---|
| Browsers | Last 2 versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari (the end-to-end tests run in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit) |
| Node.js | 18 and later for the compiler, Vite plugin, `keeno-check` and server rendering (CI tests Node 20 and 22) |
| Bun | 1.4 and later |
| Vite | 5, 6, 7 and 8 (CI builds a test app with each) |
| TypeScript | 5.0 and later |
| Editors | VS Code 1.90 and later, and editors based on it (Cursor) |
